questions.question: A porter lifts a heavy suitcase of mass $80\mathrm{kg}$ and at the destination lowers it down by a distance of $80\mathrm{cm}$ with a constant velocity. Calculate the work done by the porter in lowering the suitcase. (take $g = 9.8{\mathrm{ms}}^{ - 2}$ )
questions.explanation: {W}_{\mathrm{Porter}} + {W}_{\mathrm{mg}} = \mathrm{ΔK}.E. = 0 {W}_{\mathrm{Porter}} = - {W}_{\mathrm{mg}} = - mgh = - 80 \times 9.8 \times .8 = - 627.2J$

questions.question: Consider a force $\vec{F} = - x\hat{i} + y\hat{j}$ . The work done by this force in moving a particle from point $A\left(1,0\right)$ to $B\left(0,1\right)$ along the line segment is : (all quantities are in SI units)
questions.explanation:
It is given that a force $\vec{F} = - x\hat{i} + y\hat{j}$ acts on a particle. The particle is moved from point $A\left(1,0\right)$ to $B\left(0,1\right)$ along the line segment.

Work done by a variable force on the particle,

$W = \int \vec{F} \cdot \vec{dr} = \int \vec{F} \cdot \left(dx\hat{i} + dy\hat{j}\right)$

(In two dimension, $\vec{dr} = dx\hat{i} + dy\hat{j}$

and it is given $\vec{F} = - x\hat{i} + y\hat{j}$)

$W = \int \left( - x\hat{i} + y\hat{j}\right) \cdot \left(dx\hat{i} + dy\hat{j}\right) = \int - xdx + ydy = \int - xdx + \int ydy$.

As the particle is displaced from $A\left(1,0\right)$ to $B\left(0,1\right)$, $x$ varies from $1$ to $0$ and $y$ varies from $0$ to $1$.

So, work will be,

$W = - { \int }_{1}^{0}xdx + { \int }_{0}^{1}ydy = - {\left(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)}_{1}^{0} + {\left(\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\right)}_{0}^{1} = \frac{1}{2}\left(0 + {\left(1\right)}^{2} + {\left(1\right)}^{2} - 0\right) = 1J$.

questions.question: A uniform cable of mass $M$ and length $L$ is placed on a horizontal surface such that its {\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)}^{th}$ part is hanging below the edge of the surface. To lift the hanging part of the cable upto the surface, the work done should be:
questions.explanation: Mass of the part hanging is $\frac{M}{n}$. Centre of mass of this part lies $\frac{L}{2n}$ distance from the surface. $∴$ Work done in lifting the hanging part to surface is $W = \left(\frac{M}{n}\right) \cdot g\left(\frac{L}{2n}\right) = \frac{MgL}{2{n}^{2}}$

questions.question: A person pushes a box on a rough horizontal plateform surface. He applies a force of $200N$ over a distance of $15m$. Thereafter, he gets progressively tired and his applied force reduces linearly with distance to $100N$. The total distance through which the box has been moved is $30m$. What is the work done by the person during the total movement of the box?
questions.explanation: $W = area = (200 \times 15) + \frac{1}{2}(100 + 200) \times 15 = 3000 + 2250 W = 5250J$ ;

questions.question: A block of mass $100\mathrm{kg}$ slides over a distance of $10m$ on a horizontal surface. If the co-efficient of friction between the surfaces is $0.4$ , then the work done against friction (in $J$) is:
questions.explanation:
Given $m = 100\mathrm{kg} s = 10m \mu = 0.4$

The frictional force is given by

$\begin{matrix}f & = & \mu mg \\ & = & 0.4 \times 100 \times 10 \\ & = & 400N\end{matrix}$

So, the work done by the force can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{matrix}W & = & f \times s \\ & = & 400 \times 10 \\ & = & 4000J\end{matrix}$

questions.question: A force $\left(3 x^2+2 x-5\right) \mathrm{N}$ displaces a body from $x=2 \mathrm{~m}$ to $x=4 \mathrm{~m}$. Work done by this force is ________ $J$.

questions.question: A force $\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{x}^2 \mathrm{y} \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\mathrm{y}^2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}$ acts on a particle in a plane $\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}=10$. The work done by this force during a displacement from $(0,0)$ to $(4 \mathrm{~m}, 2 \mathrm{~m})$ is $\qquad$ Joule (round off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & y=10-x \\ & w=\int_0^4 x^2(10-x) d x+\int_0^2 y^2 d y \\ & =\frac{10 x^3}{3}-\left.\frac{x^4}{4}\right|_0 ^4+\left.\frac{y^3}{3}\right|_0 ^2 \\ & =\frac{640}{3}-\frac{256}{4}+\frac{8}{3} \\ & =216 \times 64 \\ & =152 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.question: A force $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=2 \hat{i}+\mathrm{b} \hat{j}+\hat{k}$ is applied on a particle and it undergoes a displacement $\hat{i}-2 \hat{j}-\hat{k}$. What will be the value of $b$, if work done on the particle is zero.
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & w=0 \\ & \therefore \quad \vec{F} \cdot S=0 \\ & (2 \hat{i}+b \hat{j}+\hat{k}) \cdot(\hat{i}-2 \hat{j}-\hat{k})=0 \\ & 2-2 b-1=0 \\ & b=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.question: A body of mass $0.5\mathrm{kg}$ travels on straight line path with velocity $v = \left(3{x}^{2} + 4\right)m{s}^{ - 1}$. The net work done by the force during its displacement from $x = 0$ to $x = 2m$ is
questions.explanation:
Given: $v = 3{x}^{2} + 4$

Initial and final velocities are {v}_{i} = 3{\left(0\right)}^{2} + 4 = 4m{s}^{ - 1}$

and {v}_{f} = 3{\left(2\right)}^{2} + 4 = 16m{s}^{ - 1}$

From work-energy theorem,

$\implies \Delta KE = \frac{1}{2}m\left({v}_{f}^{2} - {v}_{i}^{2}\right) \implies \Delta KE = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2}\left({16}^{2} - {4}^{2}\right) \implies \Delta KE = W = 60J$

questions.question:
Identify the correct statements from the following:

(A) Work done by a man in lifting a bucket out of a well by means of a rope tied to the bucket is negative

(B) Work done by gravitational force in lifting a bucket out of a well by a rope tied to the bucket is negative

(C) Work done by friction on a body sliding down an inclined plane is positive

(D) Work done by an applied force on a body moving on a rough horizontal plane with uniform velocity is zero

(E) Work done by the air resistance on an oscillating pendulum is negative

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Work done is given by, $W = Fs\cos \theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the force and the displacement.

case(A): Direction of force and displacement both are in the same direction and hence work done will be positive. Hence, wrong.

case(B): Direction of force and displacement both are in the opposite direction and hence work done will be negative. Hence, correct.

case(C): Direction of force and displacement both are in the opposite direction and hence work done will be negative. Hence, wrong.

case(D): Direction of force and displacement both are in the same direction and hence work done will be positive. Hence, wrong.

case(E): Direction of force and displacement both are in the opposite direction and hence work done will be negative. Hence, correct.

questions.question: A particle of mass $500g$ is moving in a straight line with velocity $v = b{x}^{\frac{5}{2}}$. The work done by the net force during its displacement from $x = 0$ to $x = 4m$ is (Take $b = 0.25{m}^{\frac{ - 3}{2}}{s}^{ - 1}$).

questions.question: A force $\vec{F} = \left(2 + 3x\right)\hat{i}$ acts on a particle in the $x$ direction where $F$ is in Newton and $x$ is in meter. The work done by this force during a displacement from $x = 0$ to $x = 4m$ is _____ $J$.
questions.explanation:
The formula to calculate the work done by a variable force is given by

$W = { \int }_{{x}_{1}}^{{x}_{2}}Fdx...\left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required work done.

$\begin{matrix}W & = & { \int }_{0}^{4}(2 + 3x)dx \\ & = & {\left(2x + \frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}\right)}_{0}^{4} \\ & = & [8 + 24]J \\ & = & 32J\end{matrix}$

questions.question: Two persons $A$ and $B$ perform same amount of work in moving a body through a certain distance $d$ with application of forces acting at angles $45 ^\circ$ and $60 ^\circ$ with the direction of displacement respectively. The ratio of force applied by person $A$ to the force applied by person $B$ is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}.$ The value of $x$ is _________.

questions.question: A small particle moves to position $5\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ from its initial position $2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$ under the action of force $5\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}N$. The value of work done will be ______ $J$.
questions.explanation:
Work done by a constant force is given by $W = \mathrm{Force}\left(\vec{F}\right) \cdot \mathrm{Displacement}\left(\vec{r}\right)$, where, $\vec{r} = {\vec{r}}_{2} - {\vec{r}}_{1}$

Given here, $\vec{{r}_{1}} = 5\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and {\vec{r}}_{2} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$

So, $W = \vec{F} \cdot \left({\vec{r}}_{2} - {\vec{r}}_{1}\right) = (5\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}) \cdot \left((5\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}) - (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k})\right) \implies W = 40J$

A force $F = (5 + 3{y}^{2})$ acts on a particle in the $y$-direction, where $F$ is newton and $y$ is in meter. The work done by the force during a displacement from $y = 2m$ to $y = 5m$ is ______ $J$.
questions.explanation:
If an object is moved by certain distance by the application of an external force along the direction of the force, then the force is said to perform some work.

Given, the force exerted on the object is

$F = 5 + 3{y}^{2}$

The formula to calculate the work done $\left(W\right)$ by the force in moving the object from a position {y}_{1}$ to another position {y}_{2}$ can be written as

$W = { \int }_{{y}_{1}}^{{y}_{2}}Fdy..........................(1)$

Substitute the values into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required work done by the force.

$\begin{matrix}W & = & { \int }_{2}^{5}\left(5 + 3{y}^{2}\right)dy \\ = {\left(5y + \frac{3{y}^{3}}{3}\right)}_{2}^{5} \\ = 132\end{matrix}$

questions.question: A small particle of mass $m$ moves in such a way that its potential energy $U = \frac{1}{2}m{\omega }^{2}{r}^{2}$ where $\omega$ is constant and $r$ is the distance of the particle from origin. Assuming Bohr’s quantization of momentum and circular orbit, the radius of {n}^{\mathrm{th}}$ orbit will be proportional to
questions.explanation:
The data given is

$U = \frac{1}{2}m{\omega }^{2}{r}^{2}$

From Bohr's quantization,

$mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi }\;$

In an orbit the value of the kinetic energy is half of the potential energy,

$K = \frac{m{\omega }^{2}{r}^{2}}{4}$

Substituting the value of equation (i) in the kinetic energy,

$K = \frac{1}{2}m\left(\frac{{n}^{2}{h}^{2}}{4{\pi }^{2}{m}^{2}{r}^{2}}\right) = \frac{m{\omega }^{2}{r}^{2}}{4}\;$

questions.question: A body is released from a height equal to the radius $\left(R\right)$ of the earth. The velocity of the body when it strikes the surface of the earth will be: (Given $g =$ acceleration due to gravity on the earth.)
questions.explanation:
Using conservation of mechanical energy,

{U}_{i} + {K}_{i} = {U}_{f} + {K}_{f} \implies - \frac{GMm}{2R} + 0 = - \frac{GMm}{R} + \frac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} \implies \frac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = \frac{GMm}{2R} \implies v = \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{R}} = \sqrt{gR}$

questions.question: An object of mass $m$ initially at rest on a smooth horizontal plane starts moving under the action of force $F = 2N$. In the process of its linear motion, the angle $\theta$ (as shown in figure) between the direction of force and horizontal varies as $\theta = kx$, where $k$ is a constant and $x$ is the distance covered by the object from its initial position. The expression of kinetic energy of the object will be $E = \frac{n}{k}\sin \theta$. The value of $n$ is ______.
questions.explanation: As seen in the free body diagram of the object, normal force $N$, weight $mg$ and force in parallel and perpendicular directions are acting. Using Newton's law of motion Along horizontal direction, $F\cos \theta = \mathrm{ma} \implies 2\cos (kx) = mv\frac{dv}{dx}$ Integrating the above relation, we have { \int }_{0}^{v}vdv = 2{ \int }_{0}^{x}\cos (kx)dx \implies \frac{m{v}^{2}}{2} = \frac{2}{k}\sin kx$ Thus, kinetic energy of the object will be $K.E. = \frac{2}{k}\sin \theta$ Thus, the value of $n = 2$.

questions.question: A boy is rolling a $0.5\mathrm{kg}$ ball on the frictionless floor with the speed of $20{ms}^{ - 1}.$ The ball gets deflected by an obstacle on the way. After deflection it moves with $5%$ of its initial kinetic energy. What is the speed of the ball now?

Initial kinetic energy $\left({k}_{i}\right) = \frac{1}{2}m{u}^{2} = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.5 \times 20 \times 20 = 100J$

After deflection it moves with $5%$ of {k}_{i} ∴{k}_{f} = \frac{5}{100} \times {k}_{i} \implies \frac{5}{100} \times 100 \implies {k}_{f} = 5J$

Now, let the final speed be $'v'{ms}^{ - 1},$ then:

{k}_{f} = 5 = \frac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} \implies {v}^{2} = 20 \implies v = \sqrt{20} = 4.47{ms}^{ - 1}$

questions.question: A wedge of mass $M = 4m$ lies on a frictionless plane. A particle of mass $m$ approaches the wedge with speed $v.$ There is no friction between the particle and the plane or between the particle and the wedge. The maximum height climbed by the particle on the wedge is given by:

questions.question: A block moving horizontally on a smooth surface with a speed of $40{ms}^{ - 1}$ splits into two equal parts. If one of the parts moves at $60{ms}^{ - 1}$ in the same direction, then the fractional change in the kinetic energy will be $x : 4$ where $x =$ ________.

questions.question: The ratio of powers of two motors is $\dfrac{3\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}+1}$, that are capable of raising 300 kg water in 5 minutes and 50 kg water in 2 minutes respectively from a well of 100 m deep. The value of $x$ will be

Required power, $P = \vec{F}.\vec{v} = \left(9{t}^{3} + 6{t}^{5}\right)W$

questions.question: A $60HP$ electric motor lifts an elevator having a maximum total load capacity of $2000kg.$ If the frictional force on the elevator is $4000N,$ the speed of the elevator at full load is close to : $\left(1\mathrm{HP} = 746W,g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}\right)$

questions.explanation:
It is given,

$v = 80\mathrm{km}{h}^{ - 1} m = 500\mathrm{kg} S = 4\mathrm{km} \mu = 0.04$

The power due to friction is

{P}_{f} = Fv$ where $F = \mu mg = \left(\left(0.04\right)\left(500 \times 9.8\right) \times 80 \times \frac{5}{18}\right)W$

Hence, the work done by the engine in overcoming the friction is

$W = {P}_{f}t = {P}_{f}\frac{d}{v} \implies W = 20 \times 9.8 \times 80 \times \frac{5}{18} \times \frac{4 \times {10}^{3}}{80 \times \frac{5}{18}} = 784\mathrm{kJ}$

questions.question: A particle of mass $m$ is moving in a circular path of constant radius $r$ such that its centripetal acceleration {a}_{c}$ is varying with time $t$ as {a}_{c} = {k}^{2}r{t}^{2}$ , where $k$ is a constant. The power delivered to the particle by the force acting on it is -
questions.explanation:
{a}_{c} = {k}^{2}r{t}^{2}$

Or $\frac{{v}^{2}}{r} = {k}^{2}r{t}^{2}$ Or $v = krt$

Therefore, tangential acceleration, {a}_{t} = \frac{dv}{dt} = kr$

Therefore, tangential force, {F}_{t} = m{a}_{t} = mkr$

Only tangential force does work.

$\text{Power} = {F}_{t}v = \left(mkr\right)\left(krt\right) \text{⇒Power} = m{k}^{2}{r}^{2}t$

questions.question: An object of mass 1000 g experiences a time dependent force $\vec{F}=\left(2 t \hat{i}+3 t^2 \hat{j}\right) N$. The power generated by the force at time $t$ is :

$\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=(2 t \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \mathrm{t} \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \mathrm{N} \\ & \mathrm{m}=1000 \mathrm{gm}=1 \mathrm{~kg} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{~F}}=m \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=2 \mathrm{t} \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \mathrm{t}^2 \hat{j} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~d} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 t \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \mathrm{t}^2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}\end{aligned} \vec{v}=t^2 \hat{i}+t^3 \hat{j}$

Power, $\mathrm{P}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}} \begin{aligned} & P=\left(2 t \hat{i}+3 t^2 \hat{j}\right) \cdot\left(t^2 \hat{i}+t^3 \hat{j}\right) \\ & P=\left(2 t^3+3 t^5\right) W\end{aligned}$

questions.question:
Water falls from a $40m$ high dam at the rate of $9 \times {10}^{4}\mathrm{kg}$ per hour. Fifty percentage of gravitational potential energy can be converted into electrical energy. Using this hydro electric energy number of $100W$ lamps, that can be lit, is

(Take $g = 10{\mathrm{ms}}^{ - 2}$)

Since $50%$ efficiency is given, half of the energy of the falling water will be used by the bulbs. Therefore,

$\frac{1}{2}\frac{ \Delta mgh}{\Delta t} = n \times P \implies \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{9 \times {10}^{4}}{3600} \times 10 \times 40 = 100n \implies n = 50$

questions.question: A body of mass 4 kg is placed on a plane at a point P having coordinate $(3,4) \mathrm{m}$. The average power and instanteous power at the end of 4 sec are in the ratio of :

questions.question:
A block of mass $5\mathrm{kg}$ starting from rest pulled up on a smooth incline plane making an angle of $30 ^\circ$ with horizontal with an effective acceleration of $1m{s}^{ - 2}$. The power delivered by the puling force at $t = 10s$ from the start is _____ $W$.

[Use $g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}$]

(Calculate the nearest integer value)
questions.explanation: Let's consider the following free-body diagram: From the above diagram, it can be written that $F - mg\sin 30 ^\circ = ma...\left(1\right)$ Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the force applied on the block. $\begin{matrix}F - 50\sin 30 ^\circ & = & 5 \times 1 \\ & \implies & F = \left(5 + 25\right)N \\ & = & 30N\end{matrix}$ The velocity of the block $\left(v\right)$ at $t = 10s$ can be written as $\begin{matrix}v & = & 0 + 1m{s}^{ - 2} \times 10s \\ & = & 10m{s}^{ - 1}\end{matrix}$ Hence, the required power is given by $\begin{matrix}P & = & Fv \\ & = & 30N \times 10m{s}^{ - 1} \\ & = & 300W\end{matrix}$

questions.question: A body of mass $2\mathrm{kg}$ is initially at rest. It starts moving unidirectionally under the influence of a source of constant power $P$. Its displacement in $4s$ is $\frac{1}{3}{\alpha }^{2}\sqrt{P}m$. The value of $\alpha$ will be ______.
questions.explanation:
Energy provided will be used to increase kinetic energy of the body. Therefore,

$\frac{1}{2}m{V}^{2} = Pt V = \sqrt{\frac{2Pt}{m}} \implies \frac{dx}{dt} = \sqrt{\frac{2Pt}{m}}\; \implies x = \sqrt{\frac{2P}{m}}\frac{2}{3}{\left({t}^{\frac{3}{2}}\right)}_{0}^{4} \implies x = \frac{16\sqrt{P}}{3} = \frac{1}{3} \times 16\sqrt{P}$

Hence, required value of $\alpha = 4$.

questions.question: If the maximum load carried by an elevator is $1400\mathrm{kg} (600\mathrm{kg}\text{-Passengers} + 800\mathrm{kg}\text{-elevator})$ , which is moving up with a uniform speed of $3m{s}^{ - 1}$ and the frictional force acting on it is $2000N$, then the maximum power used by the motor is _____________$\mathrm{kW}.\left(g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}\right)$
questions.explanation: The maximum force acting is, {F}_{max} = \left(14000 + 2000\right)N = 16000N$ The formula for power is given by, $P = {F}_{max}v$. It is given, $v = 3m{s}^{ - 1}$. $\implies P = 16000N \times 3m{s}^{ - 1} = 48000W = 48\mathrm{kW} \implies W = 48\mathrm{kW}$

questions.question: A body of mass $1\mathrm{kg}$ begins to move under the action of a time dependent force $\vec{F} = \left(t\hat{i} + 3{t}^{2}\hat{j}\right)N$, where $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ are the unit vectors along $x$ and $y$ axis. The power developed by above force, at the time $t = 2s$, will be _______$W$.
questions.explanation:
Given, $\vec{F} = \left(t\hat{i} + 3{t}^{2}\hat{j}\right)N$ and $m = 1\mathrm{kg}$

Now, we can write from Newton's second law, $\vec{F} = m\vec{a} = m\frac{d\vec{v}}{dt}$

Then, $d\vec{v} = \left(t\hat{i} + 3{t}^{2}\hat{j}\right)dt$

Integrating the above,

{ \int }_{0}^{v}d\vec{v} = { \int }_{0}^{t}\left(t\hat{i} + 3{t}^{2}\hat{j}\right)dt\;$

Now, power developed by the force is $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v} = \left(t\hat{i} + 3{t}^{2}\hat{j}\right) \cdot \left(\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}\hat{i} + {t}^{3}\hat{j}\right) = \left(\frac{{t}^{3}}{2} + 3{t}^{5}\right)$

At $t = 2s$, power is $P = \left(\frac{{2}^{3}}{2} + 3{\left(2\right)}^{5}\right) = 4 + \left(3 \times 32\right) = 100W$

questions.question: A small bob tied at one end of a thin string of length $1m$ is describing a vertical circle so that the maximum and minimum tension in the string is in the ratio $5 : 1$. The velocity of the bob at the highest position is ______ $m{s}^{ - 1}$. (Take $g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}$)
questions.explanation: Let the speed of bob at lowest position be {v}_{1}$ and at the highest position be {v}_{2}$. Maximum tension is at lowest position and minimum tension is at the highest position. Now, using, conservation of mechanical energy, $\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} = \frac{1}{2}m{v}_{2}^{2} + mg2l \implies {v}_{1}^{2} = {v}_{2}^{2} + 4gl....\left(1\right)$ Now, {T}_{\max } - mg = \frac{m{v}_{1}^{2}}{l} \implies {T}_{\max } = mg + \frac{m{v}_{1}^{2}}{l} & {T}_{\min } + mg = \frac{m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} \implies {T}_{\min } = \frac{m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} - mg \frac{{T}_{\max }}{{T}_{\min }} = \frac{5}{1} \implies \frac{mg + \frac{m{v}_{1}^{2}}{l}}{\frac{m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} - mg} = \frac{5}{1} \implies mg + \frac{m{v}_{1}^{2}}{l} = \left(\frac{m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} - mg\right)5 \implies mg + \frac{m}{l}\left({v}_{2}^{2} + 4gl\right) = \frac{5m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} - 5mg \implies mg + \frac{m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} + 4mg = \frac{5m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} - 5mg \implies 10mg = \frac{4m{v}_{2}^{2}}{l} {v}_{2} = \frac{10 \times 10 \times 1}{4}$ Thus, the velocity of the bob at the highest position is $5m{s}^{ - 1}.$

questions.question: A body of $m \mathrm{~kg}$ slides from rest along the curve of vertical circle from point $A$ to $B$ in friction less path. The velocity of the body at $B$ is: $\text { (given, } R=14 \mathrm{~m}, g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2 \text { and } \sqrt{2}=1.4 \text { ) }$
questions.explanation: Apply W.E.T. from A to B $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{mg}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{B}}-\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{A}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{mg} \times\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{2}}+\mathrm{R}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{B}}^2-0\left\{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{A}}=0 \text { rest }\right\} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{mgR} \frac{(\sqrt{2}+1)}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{B}}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{\mathrm{gR} \frac{2(\sqrt{2}+1)}{\sqrt{2}}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{10 \times 14 \times 2(2.4)}{1.4}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \\ & \Rightarrow 21.9=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \end{aligned}$

questions.question: A stone of mass $m$, tied to a string is being whirled in a vertical circle with a uniform speed. The tension in the string is

Clearly in this case, tension in the string will be minimum.

questions.question: A bob of mass $m$ is suspended at a point $O$ by a light string of length $l$ and left to perform vertical motion (circular) as shown in figure.
